target_customer: Dentists and orthodontists in Mexico and Colombia who outsource crowns, aligners and prosthetics to a lab
problem: Dental labs in Latin America worked with analog impressions, so dentists lacked a digital workflow for crowns, bridges and aligners.
business_model: Digital dental laboratory services; free intraoral scanners given in exchange for a minimum monthly lab spend
product_category: Digital dental laboratory and clinic platform

founders.name: Tommaso Tomba
previous_startups: Moons, Mexico City aligner startup (CEO per TechCrunch 2020-01-27; relation to Futura not stated in sources opened)
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder on the YC page.

founders.name: Leonardo Miron
previous_startups: Moons (named as a co-founder by Forbes Colombia 2021 per search summary; unverified)
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combines scanner hardware logistics, CAD and manufacturing workflows and a case management platform; mostly integration and operations work.

defensibility.rationale: Giving scanners tied to a minimum monthly spend creates dentist lock-in, and lab scale and quality are hard to copy quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence found that large aligner or lab players targeted the Latin American digital lab wedge or acquired Futura.

market_need_then: The company says it serves over 1,000 doctors in Mexico, Colombia and Peru; Mexico is described by a market research page as a hub for dental lab services in Latin America. Dated 2020 need evidence was not found.

branding.domain_note: Operates on futuralabs.io rather than futura.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Spanish language clinical and practical marketing with doctor testimonials

brand_strength.rationale: Brand searches mostly return a Mexican design studio also called Futura and the Futura typeface, so the name is easily confused; no brand press for the dental lab found.

outcome_analysis: Futura is an active Mexico City digital dental lab with a stated 1,000 plus doctor base across Mexico, Colombia and Peru and a listed team of about 115 on the YC page. Its funding history is not reliably public, with aggregator Series A figures that conflict, so the strength of the outcome cannot be judged. The scanner for lab spend model suggests a distribution advantage but this is not confirmed by sources.
notes: Two aggregators conflict on a Series A: VCBacked lists $7.0M in October 2023 with Alumni Ventures, Y Combinator, AlleyCorp, Carao Ventures and DILA Capital; StartupIntros lists $15.1M in May 2024 led by Alexandre Dewez. Neither is verified by a press release or second outlet, so no round is recorded and coverage is none_found. Moons shares a founder with Futura per YC listings, TechCrunch 2020-01-27 and Forbes Colombia; it is an aligner clinic business and is not listed as a competitor. Sources do not say when Futura was founded. No dated LatAm dental lab competitor source was found. Outcome search found no acquisition or layoff news. Completeness pass: press (eu-startups, tech.eu, May 2024) reports a EUR 14M Series A for an Italian edtech named Futura founded by Andrea Chirolli, Francesco Salvatore and Lorenzo Pinto; that is a different company from this YC dental lab and is not recorded here.
